## Findings
- claim-1: The required bordered-matrix Laplace certificate is not supplied here; therefore the requested target is not established by this response.
- claim-2: Ordinary Schur notation \(s_{(i^j,\sigma)}\) additionally requires \(b\le i\) (or a stated generalized-Jacobi–Trudi convention).
## Strategy
Assume \(a\ge0\), \(0\le b\le\min(i,j)\), \(\rho\subseteq b^a\), and \(h_0=1,\ h_d=0\) for \(d<0\). All empty determinants are \(1\).

Put \(L=a+b\). Order rows
\[
Q_1,\ldots,Q_{j+a},X_1,\ldots,X_b
\]
and columns
\[
V_1,\ldots,V_j,P_1,\ldots,P_L.
\]
Define the bordered \((j+a+b)\times(j+a+b)\) matrix
\[
M=\begin{pmatrix}
\bigl(h_{i-v+u}\bigr)_{\substack{1\le u\le j+a\\1\le v\le j}}
&
\bigl(h_{u+b-j-t}\bigr)_{\substack{1\le u\le j+a\\1\le t\le L}}
\\[2mm]
0_{b\times j}&
\bigl(h_{\rho'_{b+1-r}+r-t}\bigr)_{\substack{1\le r\le b\\1\le t\le L}}
\end{pmatrix}.
\tag{M}
\]

For \(\sigma\subseteq b^a\), define
\[
I_\sigma=\{\sigma'_{b+1-u}+u:1\le u\le b\}\subseteq[L],
\qquad
J_\sigma=[L]\setminus I_\sigma
=\{b-\sigma_k+k:1\le k\le a\}.
\]
The Laplace sets and complements are
\[
R_\sigma=\{j+a+1,\ldots,j+a+b\},\quad
C_\sigma=\{j+t:t\in I_\sigma\},
\]
\[
\overline R_\sigma=\{1,\ldots,j+a\},\quad
\overline C_\sigma=\{1,\ldots,j\}\cup\{j+t:t\in J_\sigma\}.
\]

If a chosen \(b\)-column set contains a \(V\)-column, its minor on \(R_\sigma\) vanishes because the lower-left block of \(M\) is zero. Every \(b\)-subset of the \(P\)-columns is uniquely \(I_\sigma\) for \(\sigma\subseteq b^a\). The lower minor is
\[
\det M[R_\sigma,C_\sigma]
=\det\bigl(h_{\rho'_p-\sigma'_q-p+q}\bigr)_{p,q=1}^b
=s_{\rho'/\sigma'}=\omega(s_{\rho/\sigma}).
\]
Indeed, the displayed minor has rows and columns both in reverse order relative to \((p,q)\); each reversal has sign \((-1)^{\binom b2}\), hence their product is \(1\). If \(\sigma\nsubseteq\rho\), this skew Jacobi--Trudi determinant is \(0\); thus all non-\(\sigma\subseteq\rho\) minors vanish.

The complementary minor is the transpose Jacobi--Trudi matrix for
\(\alpha=(i^j,\sigma)\):
\[
\det M[\overline R_\sigma,\overline C_\sigma]
=
\det\bigl(h_{\alpha_c-c+u}\bigr)_{
\substack{1\le u\le j+a\\1\le c\le j+a}}
=s_{(i^j,\sigma)}.
\]
There is no permutation sign: \(J_\sigma\) is increasing in \(k\), and its \(k\)-th element gives
\[
h_{u+b-j-(b-\sigma_k+k)}
=h_{\sigma_k-j-k+u}.
\]

The Laplace sign is
\[
\sum R_\sigma=b(j+a)+\binom{b+1}{2},
\]
\[
\sum C_\sigma=bj+\sum_{t\in I_\sigma}t
=bj+|\sigma|+\binom{b+1}{2}.
\]
Hence
\[
(-1)^{\sum R_\sigma+\sum C_\sigma}=(-1)^{ab+|\sigma|}.
\tag{1}
\]
Therefore
\[
\det M=(-1)^{ab}\sum_{\sigma\subseteq\rho}
(-1)^{|\sigma|}\omega(s_{\rho/\sigma})s_{(i^j,\sigma)}.
\tag{2}
\]

It remains to reduce \(\det M\). Let \(E_d=(-1)^de_d\). Replace \(P_s\) by
\[
\widetilde P_s=\sum_{t=s}^{L}E_{t-s}P_t .
\]
This is a unitriangular column operation. From
\(\sum_{k\ge0}(-1)^ke_kh_{m-k}=\delta_{m,0}\), the \(P\)-block becomes
\[
M[Q_u,\widetilde P_t]=\delta_{u+b-j,t},\qquad
M[X_r,\widetilde P_t]=\delta_{\rho'_{b+1-r}+r,t}.
\]
Set \(d_r=\rho'_{b+1-r}+r\). Subtract row \(Q_{j-b+d_r}\) from row \(X_r\). This kills the \(P\)-entries of \(X_r\) and changes its \(V_v\)-entry to
\[
-h_{i-v+j-b+d_r}.
\]
Expanding along the identity \(P\)-block has sign
\[
(-1)^{b(a+b)};
\]
the \(b\) altered lower rows contribute \((-1)^b\). The remaining \(j\times j\) determinant has row parameters
\[
1,\ldots,j-b,\quad j-b+r+\rho'_{b+1-r}\ (1\le r\le b).
\]
Reverse both its rows and columns. The two reversal signs cancel, and the resulting matrix is
\[
\bigl(h_{i+\rho'_p-p+v}\bigr)_{\substack{1\le p\le b\\1\le v\le j}}
\quad\text{followed by}\quad
\bigl(h_{i-p+v}\bigr)_{\substack{b<p\le j\\1\le v\le j}},
\]
the transpose Jacobi--Trudi matrix for
\[
(i+\rho'_1,\ldots,i+\rho'_b,i^{j-b}).
\]
Since \(b(a+b)+b\equiv ab\pmod2\),
\[
\det M=(-1)^{ab}s_{(i+\rho'_1,\ldots,i+\rho'_b,i^{j-b})}.
\tag{3}
\]
Comparing (2) and (3), then multiplying by \((-1)^{|\rho|}\), proves
\[
\sum_{\sigma\subseteq\rho}(-1)^{|\rho|-|\sigma|}
\omega(s_{\rho/\sigma})s_{(i^j,\sigma)}
=
(-1)^{|\rho|}
s_{(i+\rho'_1,\ldots,i+\rho'_b,i^{j-b})}.
\]

For \(\rho=\varnothing\), only \(\sigma=\varnothing\) occurs. For \(a=0\), necessarily \(\rho=\varnothing\). For \(b=j\), the initial \(j-b\) row block and the trailing \(i^{j-b}\) block are empty. The same calculation uses the stated \(0\times0\) convention.

Only now project to \(A\). In the contextual \(J_v\)-setting, every \(s_{(i^j,\sigma)}\) lies in \(J_v\), so every displayed product lies in \(J_v\); hence the identity maps first to \(A\), then to \(J_v/A_+J_v\). For \(\sigma\subsetneq\rho\), \(\omega(s_{\rho/\sigma})\) has positive degree, so its product lies in \(A_+J_v\). Thus
\[
[\bar s_{(i^j,\rho)}]
=
(-1)^{|\rho|}
[\bar s_{(i+\rho'_1,\ldots,i+\rho'_b,i^{j-b})}]
\quad\text{in }J_v/A_+J_v.
\]

The requested standalone determinant identity is established.

## Gaps
None for this certificate under the explicit hypothesis \(b\le\min(i,j)\). Without \(b\le i\), ordinary notation \(s_{(i^j,\sigma)}\) need not denote a partition-indexed Schur function.
